title: Weak homotopy retractions extend to coherent retraction diagrams
statement: Use the universes, simplicial nerves, quasicategories, coherent functors, homotopies and equivalences of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $R$ be the small ordinary category with objects $X,Y$, morphism sets $\operatorname{Hom}_R(X,X)=\{1_X,e\}$, $\operatorname{Hom}_R(X,Y)=\{r\}$, $\operatorname{Hom}_R(Y,X)=\{s\}$ and $\operatorname{Hom}_R(Y,Y)=\{1_Y\}$, and composition determined by $r\circ s=1_Y$, $s\circ r=e$, $e^2=e$, $r\circ e=r$ and $e\circ s=s$, together with the identity laws. For any quasicategory $\mathcal E$, objects $u,v\in\mathcal E$ and arrows $a:v\to u$, $b:u\to v$ whose composite $b\circ a$ is homotopic to $1_v$, there is a coherent functor $F:N(R)\to\mathcal E$ with $F(X)=u$, $F(Y)=v$, $F(s)=a$ and $F(r)=b$. More precisely, let $\operatorname{Ret}\subseteq N(R)$ be the image of the $2$-simplex with successive edges $s,r$ and long edge $1_Y$; it is $\Delta^2$ with its long edge collapsed to a point. Every simplicial map $\operatorname{Ret}\to\mathcal E$ extends to $N(R)\to\mathcal E$, retaining that whole weak-retraction triangle.

source.place: HTT Definition 4.4.5.2, Remark 4.4.5.5 and Corollary 4.4.5.7, printed pp.304-305 (PDF pp.321-322); the homotopy-category retraction criterion is explained at the start of Section 4.4.5, printed p.303. Ret to Idem+ is inner anodyne by Proposition 4.4.5.6. Read online; no local archive or matching Stacks tag.

proof.text: First fix the entire given weak-retraction triangle $f:\operatorname{Ret}\to\mathcal E$. By the nerve convention of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], a simplex of $N(R)$ is a string of composable arrows; it is nondegenerate exactly when none is an identity. For $m\geq1$, define $T_m\subseteq N(R)$ to contain the simplices whose nondegenerate strings have at most $m$ occurrences of the object $X$. Removing an identity does not affect the resulting nondegenerate string. Faces compose or delete arrows and cannot increase its number of $X$-vertices, so $T_m$ is a simplicial subset. A nondegenerate string with at most one $X$ is exactly a face of $Y\xrightarrow{s}X\xrightarrow{r}Y$ (or the vertex $Y$). Thus $T_1=\operatorname{Ret}$. Every string is finite, so $\bigcup_{m\geq1}T_m=N(R)$.

source.place: Definition 4.4.5.2 and proof of Proposition 4.4.5.6, definition of Ret(m); expanded directly as strings in the nerve; read online, archival copy WANTED; no matching Stacks tag

proof.text: For $m\geq2$, let $\tau_m:\Delta^{2m}\to N(R)$ be the alternating string $Y\xrightarrow{s}X\xrightarrow{r}Y\xrightarrow{s}\cdots\xrightarrow{r}Y$, and put $J_m=\{1,3,\ldots,2m-1\}$ and $K_m=\bigcup_{q\in J_m}\Delta^{[2m]\setminus\{q\}}$. A face missing an odd vertex has at most $m-1$ occurrences of $X$, so $\tau_m(K_m)\subseteq T_{m-1}$. A face retaining all odd vertices has $m$ occurrences of $X$ and an optional $Y$ before, between, or after them. Its consecutive arrows are $e$ between adjacent $X$ vertices, $r$ from $X$ to $Y$, and $s$ from $Y$ to $X$, so none is an identity. Distinct choices of optional even vertices give distinct nondegenerate strings. Conversely, a nondegenerate string with exactly $m$ occurrences of $X$ has no adjacent $Y$ vertices, since the only $Y$ endomorphism is $1_Y$; its intervening and endpoint $Y$ vertices give exactly this unique choice. Hence $\tau_m$ bijects the nondegenerate simplices outside $K_m$ with those of $T_m$ outside $T_{m-1}$. For degenerate simplices the same assertion follows by inserting identities at the specified positions. The map from the degreewise pushout $T_{m-1}\amalg_{K_m}\Delta^{2m}$ to $T_m$ is therefore bijective in every degree and respects all operators. This proves the required pushout identification without assuming $\tau_m$ is injective on $K_m$.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 4.4.5.6, pushout square for Ret(m-1) into Ret(m), with its nerve-string verification written out; read online, archival copy WANTED; no matching Stacks tag

proof.text: Suppose inductively that $f_{m-1}:T_{m-1}\to\mathcal E$ has been chosen, starting with $f_1=f$. The subset $J_m$ has the gap $1<2<3$, with $1,3\in J_m$ and $2\notin J_m$. Apply [lem-coef-gapped-face-inner-horn-presentation] with $n=2m$, $J=J_m$, and $Q=\mathcal E$ to the map $f_{m-1}\tau_m|_{K_m}$. It gives $g_m:\Delta^{2m}\to\mathcal E$ agreeing with that map on all of $K_m$. The pushout identification proved in step 2 now glues $g_m$ and $f_{m-1}$ to a simplicial map $f_m:T_m\to\mathcal E$ whose restriction is exactly $f_{m-1}$. This constructs the compatible sequence by induction on $m$.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 4.4.5.6, application of Lemma 4.4.5.8 to the odd-vertex subset; Corollary 4.4.5.7, extension; read online, archival copy WANTED; no matching Stacks tag

proof.text: Define $F$ on a simplex of $N(R)$ to be its image under any $f_m$ with that simplex in $T_m$. The exact restriction equalities make this independent of $m$. Since each $T_m$ is a simplicial subset and each $f_m$ is a simplicial map, $F$ commutes with every face and degeneracy. It is therefore a coherent functor in the sense of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. On $T_1=\operatorname{Ret}$ it equals the original $f$ exactly. In particular it retains the given two edges and their entire triangle. Only a union of small simplicial sets and a recursive choice of horn fillers was used; no colimits in $\mathcal E$ were assumed.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 4.4.5.6, infinite union Ret(1) into Ret(2) into ..., and Corollary 4.4.5.7; read online, archival copy WANTED; no matching Stacks tag

proof.text: For the first formulation, fill the inner $2$-horn with successive edges $a:v\to u$ and $b:u\to v$, obtaining a triangle with long edge $c:v\to v$. The homotopy-category composition statement of [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition] identifies $[c]=[b][a]$, so the hypothesis gives $[c]=[1_v]$ in the right-pinched mapping space. That space is Kan by [lem-coef-infinity-pinch-comparison]. By [lem-coef-kan-realization-serre], realization components of this Kan complex are exactly vertices modulo finite edge zigzags. In a Kan complex a finite edge zigzag can be made into one oriented edge: reverse an edge by filling an outer $2$-horn with an identity edge, and concatenate edges by filling an inner $2$-horn. Thus choose an edge from $1_v$ to $c$ in this mapping space. By the right-pinched definition in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], it is a triangle with successive edges $(1_v,c)$ and long edge $1_v$.

source.place: Section 4.4.5 opening retraction criterion and Remark 4.4.5.5; expanded using existing mapping-space composition and Kan comparison nodes; read online, archival copy WANTED; no matching Stacks tag

proof.text: Use vertices $(v,v,u,v)$ of a $3$-simplex. Prescribe its face $d_0$ to be the triangle $(a,b,c)$ just chosen, its face $d_2$ to be the triangle $(1_v,c,1_v)$ just chosen, and its face $d_3$ to be the degeneracy of $a$ with successive edges $(1_v,a)$ and long edge $a$. Their common edges agree: they form an inner horn $\Lambda^3_1\to\mathcal E$. By the quasicategory definition of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], fill this horn. The remaining face $d_1$ is a triangle with successive edges $(a,b)$ and long edge $1_v$. Since this last edge is degenerate, its map $\Delta^2\to\mathcal E$ factors through the quotient $\operatorname{Ret}$ collapsing that edge. Apply steps 1-4 to this map. The extension has $F(X)=u$, $F(Y)=v$, $F(s)=a$ and $F(r)=b$, as required.

lean.statement: theorem weak_retraction_coherent_extension : (∀ (E : SSet.{u}) [Quasicategory E] (u v : E _⦋0⦌) (a b : E _⦋1⦌), E.δ 1 a = v → E.δ 0 a = u → E.δ 1 b = u → E.δ 0 b = v → (∃ (c : E _⦋1⦌) (t : E _⦋2⦌), E.δ 2 t = a ∧ E.δ 0 t = b ∧ E.δ 1 t = c ∧ WeakRetractionEdgeHomotopic c (E.σ 0 v)) → ∃ F : weakRetractionBase ⟶ E, F.app (op ⦋0⦌) (ComposableArrows.mk₀ ((AsSmall.up (C := WeakRetractionObject)).obj WeakRetractionObject.X)) = u ∧ F.app (op ⦋0⦌) (ComposableArrows.mk₀ ((AsSmall.up (C := WeakRetractionObject)).obj WeakRetractionObject.Y)) = v ∧ F.app (op ⦋1⦌) (ComposableArrows.mk₁ ((AsSmall.up (C := WeakRetractionObject)).map weakRetractionS)) = a ∧ F.app (op ⦋1⦌) (ComposableArrows.mk₁ ((AsSmall.up (C := WeakRetractionObject)).map weakRetractionR)) = b) ∧ (∀ (E : SSet.{u}) [Quasicategory E] (f : weakRetractionRet ⟶ E), ∃ F : weakRetractionBase ⟶ E, weakRetractionRetInclusion ≫ F = f)
